sub_answers.sub_question: List the federal grant programs, formula and discretionary funding streams, and financial assistance mechanisms managed by the U.S. Department of Transportation between 2013 and 2017 while Anthony Foxx served as Secretary (for example: TIGER, FASTLANE, FAA airport grants, FTA urbanized area formula grants, transit capital investment grants).
sub_answers.text: The Department of Transportation allocated discretionary grant funding through Infrastructure Investments/Discretionary Grants delegated in the Consolidated Appropriations Act of 2014.[d58235s2p0] The DOT administered project-specific transit capital grants such as the Capital Investment Grants (CIG) program administered by the Federal Transit Administration.[d74699486s21p0] The DOT awarded American Recovery and Reinvestment Act transit funds to major projects in 2012, including light rail, commuter rail, heavy rail, subway, and bus rapid transit projects.[d58235s2p0] The DOT operated formula and discretionary grant programs funded through multi-year federal transportation authorizations and annual appropriations, reflected in its Fiscal Year 2016 budget authorization and multi-year funding under the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act funding period 2022–2026 noted in budget history.[d58235s2p0]

sub_answers.text: The Federal Aviation Administration sponsored the Airport Cooperative Research Program (ACRP) administered through TRB [d5772843s4p0]. The Federal Highway Administration sponsored the National Cooperative Highway Research Program (NCHRP) in partnership with state departments of transportation and AASHTO [d5772843s4p0]. The Federal Transit Administration sponsored the Transit Cooperative Research Program (TCRP) administered under a three-way agreement with the National Academy of Sciences, the Transit Development Corporation, Inc., and the American Public Transportation Association [d5772843s4p0]. TRB and the National Academies received support from the various administrations of the U.S. Department of Transportation for selective research funding through NCHRP, ACRP, and TCRP [d5772843s4p0].

Which cross-agency or stakeholder bodies, advisory committees, working groups, interagency task forces, or public-private partnerships did Secretary Anthony Foxx create, chair, or rely on to coordinate transportation policy and implementation at USDOT (e.g., modal councils, National Freight Advisory Committee-type entities, grant review panels, or coordination with DOT’s modal administrations)?
sub_answers.text: TRB cooperative research programs used industry leaders who served as references during projects [d5772843s4p0]. The Transit Cooperative Research Program (TCRP) was carried out under a three-way agreement among the National Academy of Sciences, the Transit Development Corporation, Inc., and the American Public Transportation Association [d5772843s4p0]. TRB programs facilitated projects with support from external organizations such as the Governors Highway Safety Association for the Behavioral Traffic Safety Cooperative Research Program (BTSCRP) [d5772843s4p0].
